briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 escalate AGI capabilities race amid compute shortages

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The frontier AI race has intensified with multiple model releases from US and Chinese labs this month. Compute constraints and safety concerns are shaping strategic decisions across governments and corporations. Prompt injection attacks continue to expose production systems to manipulation.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI shipped o4 with advanced reasoning while Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus. Google deployed Gemini 3 and Meta open-sourced Llama 4. xAI's Grok-3 and DeepSeek R2 highlight the accelerating multi-polar competition.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. Regulators in EU and US are advancing mandatory red-teaming rules. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp is behind schedule while Microsoft and Google announce new 100k H100 clusters. TSMC reports record AI chip orders for Q3.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
